name: Electric Border
description: WebGL2 wrapper that draws a living electric border of glowing, jittering strands and random sparks around its children, reacting to the cursor and clicks with heat and pulses.
contents: Container div wrapping the children with a rounded border radius
Absolutely positioned WebGL canvas extending 64px beyond the container on every side, drawing the electric border
behavior: Several noise-driven strands wobble along the rounded rectangle edge with glow and flicker
Random sparks arc off the border, more often near the cursor
Cursor near the container adds a smoothly following heat spot that brightens and adds strands
Click on the container sends a pulse wave along the border and spawns a spark
Intro reveal sweeps the border in around the perimeter, and toggling active fades it out or back in
Pauses rendering when offscreen or tab hidden, recovers from WebGL context loss
Reduced motion preference slows animation, disables sparks, pulses and flicker
editableByProps: Border color and separate glow color
Animation speed, chaos, spread, thickness, strand count (1 to 6), glow, intensity, flicker
Spark frequency, corner radius, border offset from the box
Turning the effect on or off, intro reveal, cursor and click interaction, cursor heat radius
Dark or light theme rendering, wrapper className and style

needsCodeEdit.change: Change number of simultaneous sparks or click pulses
needsCodeEdit.where: ARCS and PULSES constants at the top of the file

needsCodeEdit.change: Change how far the effect extends beyond the container
Change the core color brightness relative to color
needsCodeEdit.where: core calculation in the settings object inside ElectricBorder

fixed: Requires WebGL2, renders nothing if unavailable or if shader compile fails
Listens to pointermove and pointerdown on window for the whole page while mounted
Canvas extends 64px outside the container, so parents must not clip overflow and neighbors need spacing
Canvas pixel count is capped by a 3 million pixel budget and device pixel ratio capped at 2
Content is not styled, the component draws only the border and the children define the box size
Uses Tailwind classes (relative, isolate, absolute, z-[1], pointer-events-none) on the wrapper and canvas
Border color is additive light on a transparent canvas, so it reads best on dark backgrounds unless theme is light
Heavy shader work on every frame, costly on low-end mobile GPUs and many instances

options.look: Additive glowing light strands with bright cores, best on dark backgrounds
options.useWhen: The page background is dark or saturated

options.look: Ink-like opaque colored strands with a darker blended color for visibility
